families.why: both make something bad less bad: alleviate = pain, suffering, pressure; mitigate = the harm or risk of something
less bad vs worse: the same situations, opposite direction
both reduce something harmful: curb limits it, mitigate softens its effects
both keep bad behaviour down: curb limits it, deter puts people off doing it
both reduce a harm's effect: offset balances it with something positive
both 'make more so': enhance something good, exacerbate something already bad
make a process easier vs get in its way
both damage progress: hinder slows it, undermine weakens it from below
both stop things happening: hinder blocks the process, deter discourages the person
look alike (under-) but mean the opposite: weaken vs support from below
both make a process smoother: streamline by cutting steps out
all mean helping something along: ease a process, grow it over time, improve what is already good
both start with f- and are about growth: you foster something so that it flourishes
both mean doing very well: thrive on = do well because of hard conditions
grow strongly vs shrink steadily
all about how widespread something is: ubiquitous = literally everywhere, prevalent = common in a place or time
same root: adjective vs noun
both start pre- and mean 'mostly / common'
being everywhere vs spreading into every part
sound alike (-iquitous / -iguous), unrelated meanings
both differences: disparity = unfair gap between groups, discrepancy = things that should match but don't
same root: an unfair gap vs very different things
sound almost the same; very different vs hopeless
both des- and both bleak: hopeless and ready to try anything vs empty and abandoned
both about inequality of size: too big or small relative to something vs a gap between groups
too small to matter vs large and important
both about size: large vs out of balance with something else
long in- adverbs ending -ly: by nature, always, by accident
look alike and overlap: always happens vs certain to happen
both -ly adverbs of degree: by nature vs mostly
both introduce a contrast: the opposite side vs a surprising contradiction
both concede a point: in spite of / although
both hedge a claim: you can argue it vs it seems likely
same root: noun vs adverb
both about two things in tension: self-contradiction vs a split into two opposites
both about kinship: a natural liking vs being similar
both about convincing: plausible = believable, compelling = so strong you can't ignore it
both 'could work / could be true': viable = works in practice, plausible = seems true
all about what works in practice: works at all, keeps working over time, a practical attitude
can succeed vs has no chance
both unclear: ambiguous wording vs unclear rules
all im-p...: an effect, a likely consequence, to put into action
both 'very important': pivotal = everything turns on it, profound = deep in effect
rhyme (-ocate): argue for vs give out
both about deciding where time or resources go
both det-, both negative: discourage vs harmful
makes people act vs puts them off
per-...-ate: keep something going vs spread through it
both improve a system: rebuild it completely vs simplify it
all trigger change: a trigger, shock into action, a shock that makes you change
both sudden realisations: an inner insight vs an outside shock
all about agreeing: group agreement vs shared understanding vs personal agreement
both about reaching agreement: bring sides together vs the agreement itself
doing less than needed vs more than needed vs careful about every detail
both about detail: intricate things vs meticulous people
complex and detailed vs basic and undeveloped
both boring: tedious = long and repetitive, mundane = ordinary everyday
both describe tough tasks: boring and slow vs hard and tiring
both about hard tasks: daunting before you start, arduous while you do it
both 'too much': daunting saps confidence beforehand, overwhelming is more than you can cope with
both withstand pressure: resilience = bounce back (people), robust = strong (systems, evidence)
both re-l... and about persistence: bounce back vs never stop
stages of learning a skill: lots to learn, starting to manage, automatic
both: something with a good and a bad side
both 'a blessing...': bad that turns out good vs good and bad at once
both about downsides: a disadvantage vs giving one thing up to gain another
both advantages vs having to give one up

words: take it with a pinch of salt
families.why: how to treat what you hear: doubt it vs think about it seriously
both about feelings and memories: evoke brings one to mind, resonate means it strikes a chord and stays
both bright: vivid colours and images vs a soft glow
both longing: yearn for anything, nostalgic for the past
both eph-/epi- and both brief: lasting a short time vs a sudden realisation
short 'b... the ...' idioms: relax people at the start vs force yourself to do something unpleasant
describing a place: calm vs disordered vs empty and bleak (serene and desolate are both quiet)

speak.prompt: Describe a time you had too much to do at work or university. How did you decide what to do first, and was anything left out?
Talk about someone you have worked with who always did more than they had to. What did they do, and how did others react?
Some people prefer a job with lots of freedom, others prefer clear instructions. Which suits you better, and what are the downsides?
Describe a skill you found hard at first but can now do without thinking. How long did it take, and what helped?
Talk about a subject or course that turned out to be much harder than you expected. What made it difficult?
Describe a book, talk or lesson that changed the way you think about something. Why did it stay with you?
Talk about an environmental problem in the place where you grew up. What causes it, and what could reduce it?
Should people be rewarded or punished to change their habits, for example plastic use or driving? Which works better, and why?
Describe a moment that made you realise you needed to change a habit, such as how much you spend, waste or travel.
Describe a piece of technology you use every day. In what ways has it made your life better, and in what ways worse?
Talk about a trend you saw spread online. Why do you think people joined in, and how long did it last?
How do you decide whether to believe something you read online? Give an example of a time you got it wrong or right.
Describe a time you disagreed with a friend or relative and later made up. How did you get back on good terms?
Talk about someone you clicked with straight away. What did you have in common, and how did you first start talking?
In a group, how do you usually reach a decision everyone accepts? Describe a time it worked well or badly.
Describe a place, song or smell that brings back strong memories. What does it remind you of, and how does it make you feel?
Talk about one of the most exciting experiences of your life. What happened, and why was it so memorable?
Describe a moment when you suddenly understood something about yourself. What led to it, and what changed afterwards?
Describe a place you have visited that felt completely calm. What was it like, and how did it compare with where you live?
Talk about the city you live in or know best. What are its good and bad sides, and would you like to live somewhere quieter?
Do you prefer to plan a trip in detail or decide as you go? Describe a trip where your approach worked or went wrong.
Describe a time a plan went badly wrong. What made it worse, and what did you learn?
Talk about a problem you solved in a practical, not perfect, way. Why did you choose that solution?
Describe a time you made a situation worse without meaning to. What happened, and how did you fix it?
Some people say it is better to have one career for life, others say it is better to change often. What is your view, and what would the other side say?
Talk about an opinion you used to hold but have changed. What convinced you, and do you still see some truth in your old view?
Is it better to grow up in a big family or a small one? Give your view, an example, and the strongest argument against it.
Describe a change you have noticed in your town or among people you know over the last ten years. How big is it, and what caused it?
Talk about a time two pieces of information, such as a bill and a receipt, did not match. How did you notice and what did you do?
Do people of different ages in your country spend their free time differently? Describe the main differences and what explains them.
Describe a turning point in your life. What triggered it, and how did things change afterwards?
Talk about something that changed suddenly in your town, school or workplace. How did people react at first, and in the long term?
Which recent change in daily life do you think is here to stay, and which will fade? Explain why.
Describe a difficult period in your life and how you got through it. What helped you keep going?
Talk about something unpleasant you had to make yourself do. Why did you put it off, and how did it go?
Describe a setback that turned out to be a good thing in the end. How did you see it then, and how do you see it now?
